title: plugin-detail: an authored `sections[].group` THROWS and takes every sibling section down (both the spec's and this renderer's own docs predict a silent no-op), and an enumerated `sections[].fields` resolves labels only through the i18n bundle — with none, every app shows raw field names
body:
Renderer half of **objectstack#16695**, filed by the triage seat so the work sits in the repo that owns `RecordDetailsRenderer`. That card stays open in objectstack for the spec-side half (whether `group` should keep being declared on `record:details` while no renderer implements it).

⛔ Filed unassigned. The browser measurements are the original reporter's (`objectstack-ai/hotclm`, `@objectstack/*` 17.3.0, `@objectstack/console` as shipped); ⛔ I did not re-drive a browser. The in-tree readings below are mine and are marked as such.

## Finding 1 — `group` is documented as "not read", and it throws

Authoring a complete, spec-valid section `{ group: 'parties' }` on `record:details` produces:

```
Component "record:details" failed to render — Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')
```

Not the section — **the whole component**, taking every sibling section with it.

⭐ **Two independent documents both predict the milder failure, and both are wrong.**

**This repo's own props description** (`packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx:451`, verbatim):

> Two are declared upstream and **NOT read here**: `group`, which objectui does not implement on a detail section, and `hideEmpty`, deliberately retired in objectui#7129 … **authoring it does nothing on this renderer.**

**objectstack's spec docblock for #13855** (`packages/spec/src/data/field-group-layout.ts:45-47`, verbatim):

> the reference surface would accept a key the declaring surface refuses, so the reference could never resolve and **the section would render nothing with nothing reported**.

⇒ "not read", "does nothing", "renders nothing" — three phrasings of a no-op, across two repos. The shipped behaviour is a **crash**. **"Not implemented" and "throws" are different contracts**, and every written record of this key asserts the safe one.

My in-tree reading, `objectui origin/main`:

```
git grep -n '\.group\b' packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx   ->  0 (no match)
control: grep -c 'sections'  same file                          ->  9   (the instrument fires)
```

⇒ the key is genuinely never read. The crash therefore comes from downstream code assuming every section has the shape a `name`/`fields` section has — consistent with objectstack#11289's independently recorded reading that the renderer maps every authored section through `s.name`, and with `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.sectionHeadingsRenderPath-6190.test.tsx:53`'s `sectionLabel(objectName, s.name, rawTitle ?? s.name)`.

## Finding 2 — enumerated `fields` resolves labels ONLY through the i18n bundle

Originally filed as "renders raw keys"; **sharpened by the reporter** in objectstack#16695 comment `5578258335` after a second run disagreed with the first. The variable neither run controlled was the translation bundle:

- On a tree with **no** `i18n` block and no `translations:` (`hotclm` @ `0a61743`), the DOM text is the field **name** — `term_months`, `auto_renew`, lowercase with underscores, under a CSS `text-transform: uppercase`. `Our Signing Entity` is **absent from the page**, though `clm_contract.our_entity` declares exactly that as its `label`.
- After the app added a bundle key `objects.clm_contract.fields.our_entity.label`, the section began rendering labels.

> An enumerated `sections[].fields` list resolves its field labels **only through the translation bundle**. With no bundle key it falls back to the raw field **name**, not to the `label:` the object declares.

⇒ **every app with no translations configured shows raw field names on its detail pages**, and `validate` / `lint` report nothing.

**The declared-label path demonstrably exists**: the platform's own *synthesized* default record page renders declared labels (`REGISTRATION / TAX ID`, `LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE`) for a different object in the same app. It reaches them by a different path — the **group-derived** one, which is the path Finding 1 throws on.

⇒ One story: **the group-derived body is the maintained one; the author-enumerated body is second-class in both of its spellings** — one throws, the other loses labels. So this is likely a missing fallback, not a missing capability.

## Acceptance

1. **Finding 1 — decide the contract, then make the code and the docs agree.** Either implement `group`, or make an unimplemented `group` a real no-op (the behaviour both documents already promise). ⛔ What must not survive is today's state, where the code throws and every written record says it does nothing. If the choice is no-op, the section should still be visible to the author as unrendered — ⛔ silently dropping an authored section is the failure objectstack's own docblock was written to avoid.
2. **A crashing section must never take its siblings down.** Independent of `group`: one malformed section should degrade to that section, not to `Component "record:details" failed to render`. This is the acceptance criterion with the widest reach and it should have its own test — ⛔ it is not satisfied by fixing `group` alone.
3. **Finding 2 — fall back to the declared `label:` before the field name.** Order: i18n bundle key → object's declared `label` → field name. Assert all three rungs, ⛔ not just the first and last.
4. **The two bodies must agree.** Same object, same fields, authored once as a group reference and once as an enumerated list: identical rendered labels. Today the synthesized (group-derived) page and the enumerated section disagree, which is what let this ship.
5. **Negative controls**: an app **with** a full bundle must be unchanged by (3); a field with **no** declared `label` must still fall back to its name; a well-formed section must be unaffected by (2).
6. `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx:451`'s description string is part of the deliverable — it currently tells authors `group` "does nothing", which is false today and must be true (or replaced) when this lands.

## Boundaries

- ⛔ One app, one console build. Re-confirm against a current `@objectstack/console` — a shipped-bundle read is how objectstack#11289 pinned its half.
- ⛔ Finding 2's control set is two surfaces in one app. If the enumerated form resolves labels correctly somewhere else, that narrows this to an unisolated condition and the card should say so rather than be closed.
- ⛔ Do not fold in `hideEmpty` — deliberately retired in objectui#7129 (maintainer 2026-09-01); it is named beside `group` in the same sentence and is **not** the same question.

Related: objectstack#16695 (the filing, spec-side half stays there) · objectstack#13855 (the `group` reference form) · objectstack#11289 (`s.name` mapping; `hideEmpty`/`collapsible`/`showBorder` honoured but undeclared) · objectstack#5611 (`sections` string form retired) · objectui#6190 (section-heading render path) · objectui#7129 (`hideEmpty` retirement)
